IN PHOTOS: Reminder signs will be posted at the corner of H.S Lacson and Dimasalang in Sampaloc, Manila, as well as alternate routes for motorists to take during the closure of the Northbound Dimasalang. 

The Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) is scheduled to close the northbound lane of the Dimasalang Bridge along Dimasalang Street in Sampaloc, Manila starting May 23, 2026 for the second phase of its rehabilitation and major repair works. 

The Project aims to ensure the structural integrity, safety, and continued usability of the bridge for the motoring public and nearby communities. Motorists are advised to observe the full traffic rerouting plan, which will be published by the city government on its official social media platforms.

📸: Norman Cruz

#MSNews | Paghahanda sa Tag-ulan

The city government of Manila continues to make its preparations for the rainy season ahead of back-to-school in June. 

Mayor Francisco Moreno Domagoso told Manila City Hall Press Club (MCHPC) shared that their target is for the flood to subside along with the cessation of the downpour. 

He also stressed the vital role of Metropolitan Manila Development Authority’s (MMDA) pumping station in the city to prevent any possible flooding. | via Pot Chavez

📸: Pot Chavez

🚛 Diversions will be in place for heavy vehicles including lorries, tippers, tankers, private buses, tractors, JCBs, etc.
⚠️ Citizens are advised to:
✅ Avoid Uppal Junction and surrounding congested routes
✅ Use alternative routes & ORR wherever possible
✅ Prefer Metro Rail 🚇 and RTC buses 🚌
✅ Follow traffic diversions and parking instructions
🅿️ Spectators are requested to use designated parking areas only.
📍Pass Holders Parking:
• A Ground Parking (Entry through Gate 1A only)

• Penguin Parking Area & TGIALA Parking Area
